description.narrative:
The project is a joint programme with six participating UN organisations (PUNO’s): FAO, UNDP, UNFPA, UN Habitat, UNICEF and WFP.
The overall goal of the project is that the local socio-economic situation is improved, inequalities reduced, and urban-rural linkages strengthened in a sustainable manner.
The project outcomes are: 1. Women, men, girls and boys have more equitable basic services, such as electricity, water, education and health care. 2. Women, men, including youth have enhanced sustainable food systems and livelihood opportunities. 3. Trust, cohesion, and cross-cleavage cooperation between local communities is enhanced.
The project has an area-based approach and will start with the population in Aleppo which is home to about 4.2 million Syrians. Norway att MFA has previously supported the first phase of the Programme (UNJP 1.0).
FAO is at the forefront of work towards sustainable agriculture by promoting protection and sustainable use of natural resources while meeting society’s growing needs for decent and resilient livelihoods. UNDP is a leading agency with its in-house capacity in conflict sensitivity. In addition, UNDP has extensive experience in programming to support access to livelihoods and basic services across Syria. UNFPA works extensively to achieve gender equality through gender mainstreaming and gender equality programming. UNFPA also supports women empowerment interventions. UN Habitat’s work around area-based planning offers a useful framework for local actors, local communities, local leaders etc. to develop plans through participatory, inclusive, and bottom-up processes. UNICEF works to ensure and support the protection of children’s rights, including equitable access for girls, boys, and young people to basic services. WFP works with its expertise and demonstrated capacity, in close coordination with FAO++, in developing value chains on key agriculture commodities for livelihoods and economic recovery.
